reason: The picture connects these messengers with activating muscle genes in the unspecialized cells, which should help reach the muscle RNA goal.
expectation: The messengers will help a group of cells activate muscle-related instructions.

alternatives.reason: The supporting-cell path also matches a goal, but I can start with muscle.

effect: The muscle messengers produced cells with muscle-protein RNA, revealing a goal to build pulling proteins.
reaction: The picture makes the next step clearer: the RNA is ready, but the proteins are not made yet.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells have the RNA instructions for muscle proteins.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to build muscle pulling proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the supporting-cell path instead.

effect: The muscle cells now contain pulling proteins, completing that goal; the support-protein RNA goal remains.
reaction: The sliding fibres give a useful picture of how the proteins help shorten a cell.
reason: The supporting-cell messengers are pictured activating support-protein genes in the unspecialized population.
expectation: A group of cells will make RNA copies of support-protein instructions.

effect: The supporting cells now have RNA instructions, and the new goal is to build fibres around them.
reaction: The picture makes it clear that the fibres have not been built yet.
reason: As with the muscle proteins, amino acids are the building blocks needed to follow the RNA instructions.
expectation: The cells will make supporting protein fibres around themselves.

effect: The supporting cells made connective tissue around themselves, completing the final goal and showing a contrast with muscle cells keeping pulling proteins inside.
reaction: The contrast between proteins inside cells and fibres around them was satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building both kinds of proteins was most worthwhile because it showed how cells with the same DNA can do different jobs.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second amino-acid combination felt a little repetitive after the muscle path, though its result added a useful contrast.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the supporting cells released proteins to build material around themselves, rather than keeping them inside like the muscle cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary: the messenger pictures named the genes they affected, and amino acids were identified as protein building blocks.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because seeing how these different cells contribute to larger structures sounds interesting.
